Concept 6 · the .bin file flows along one guarded road: from the admin to Node 1's other shelf

guard
what is refused (exact wording)
Admin on /fleet
dashboard 1.4.0
only an admin account may upload (login cookie)
straight from the browser, without copying files to the server
viewer → 403
no login → 401
The backend accepts
the first byte must be 0xE9 (an ESP32 app image)
at most 1,966,080 bytes (one shelf); a body over 2 MiB refused
one version = one file, never overwritten; SHA-256 computed by the server
413 (more than 2 MiB)
firmware-data cupboard
the backend's Docker cupboard
mounted only on the backend, not on web: Caddy doesn't serve it
not in Git: *.bin, firmware-data/, firmware/**/build/
why: Node 1's .bin holds what keys.h holds (the ESP-NOW key, the portal password)
no public address for this cupboard
Route /fw/node-1/<version>.bin
Caddy forwards to the backend
Basic device_id:key matched (matchKey, the Module 21 promise)
x-ESP32-STA-MAC must equal device_id
a deactivated device refused; a withdrawn release not served
at most 120 requests per minute per IP address
the same version as x-ESP32-version → 304 (no content): not downloaded
Node 1 1.7.0
before and after downloading
url must be the stored server address + /fw/node-1/<version>.bin
https:// + the built-in CA bundle (with ISRG Root X1 and X2): chain + name
http:// only to a home IP address
the file's SHA-256 = the command's sha256; versions below 1.7.0 refused

text.tspan: url is not this home's server
http only for the home network

svg.text: into the other shelf
Who tries, what stops them
simulated lab: simulator; 1.7.1 real + fake files
a stranger who knows the /fw/… address
the device key (403); the file is never public
another board asking for the file as Node 1
Node 1's own key + MAC (403)
a fake cmd update pointing at another server
Node 1 refuses (url is not this home's server): the key isn't sent
a file in the cupboard changed by one byte
the command's SHA-256 fingerprint: not installed, the old shelf stays
an eavesdropper on the internet road
https://; http:// only on the home Wi-Fi
another device account wanting to read Node 1's cmd
device accounts' default read permission = deny (only its own cmd)
SHA-256 isn't a signature: it proves the file is intact, not who made it. The backend and Node-RED may give the command, but only
for a file on that home server itself. Digital signatures (Secure Boot, signed updates) are covered in the Technical Deep Dive
HTTPS in the esp32 package 3.3.12 checks the certificate chain and the server name, but not its validity dates: no need to wait for the internet clock
(from the settings of the esp32 package 3.3.12; not tested by the author on a board)
